newsitem.title: TURKEY: German foreign minister Kinkel to visit Turkey.
newsitem.headline: German foreign minister Kinkel to visit Turkey.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel will visit Turkey next week for talks on Ankara's long-standing bid for European Union membership, a Turkish foreign ministry official said on Wednesday.
"(Kinkel) is coming on the 25th and leaving on the 27th... European Union and bilateral relations will be discussed," the official told Reuters.

Turkey has been an associate member of the European Union since 1963 and applied for full membership in 1987. But it has seen much of Eastern Europe and adversary Cyprus jump it in the queue of EU candidates in recent years.
The EU has kept Turkey at arm's length due to Ankara's human rights record, the divided island of Cyprus and disputes with member Greece.

Ankara was snubbed earlier this month by a meeting of Christian Democrat EU leaders, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, at which members agreed Ankara could never be a candidate to join the European club.
But EU foreign ministers last week assured Ankara that the door was still open for membership of the 15-nation bloc.
Germany is home to about two million people from Turkey, including around 500,000 Kurds.
